candidates.name: Katedrala sv. Duje
candidates.content: Built around 305 AD as a mausoleum of Roman emperor Diocletian's (the oldest cathedral building in the world). The cathedral is also a very beautiful mixture of Roman temple and Catholic church. It also has a beautiful belltower w

candidates.name: Archaeological Museum
candidates.content: The oldest museum in Croatia (1820), about 20 min walk north of the old town. Many artifacts and monuments from Roman colonies Salona and Narona. Most of the panel information is only in Croatian, so use a translator app or bring

candidates.name: Jupiter temple
candidates.content: Ancient Roman temple which became St. John's church.

candidates.name: Peristylium
candidates.content: Main square of Diocletian's palace with well preserved Roman architecture.

candidates.name: Galerija Meštrović
candidates.content: The gallery contains works of Ivan Meštrović, famous Croatian sculptor.

candidates.name: St. Duje's bell tower
candidates.content: Beautiful belltower which provides you a great panoramic view of Split, nearby islands and Marjan hill. The ascent is certainly not for those with vertigo, but the views from the top are marvelous. It costs €1.40 to go up the bell

candidates.name: Basement halls of Diocletian's Palace
candidates.content: Exceptionally well preserved substructure of Diocletian's Palace now open as a museum. One of the locations in Game of Thrones. It's strongly recommended to book a tour guide, otherwise visitors walk through mostly empty halls wit

candidates.name: Getski vrtal
candidates.content: It is the smallest park in Split, situated in the Diocletian's palace at the Dominisova street (Marko Antonio De Dominis street). In that park are beautiful traditional Dalmatian tiramolas. During the summer these are full of clot

candidates.name: Froggyland
candidates.content: A strange museum for 21 dioramas of taxidermy frogs in a variety of everyday human situations, crafted in the early 1900s.

candidates.name: Old graveyards
candidates.content: Sustipan and old Jewish cemetery

candidates.name: HNK Hajduk Split
candidates.content: They play in Prva HNL, the top tier of football in Croatia; indeed they've never been out of it, and have won it several times. Their home ground of Poljud stadium (capacity 34,000) is 1 km north of the main bus station, harbour a

candidates.name: Beach at Bačvice
candidates.content: This beach has beautiful fine-grained sand, and it is very shallow. There are many cafes and places to eat ice cream. It is certainly not the best beach in Croatia (it is packed solid most of summer), but it will give you a feelin

candidates.name: Split city beach
candidates.content: If you have a longer stop-over in Split, 5 min south of the passenger terminal and the train and bus stations lies Split's city beach where you can take a plunge in the Adriatic.

candidates.name: Picigin
candidates.content: Traditional beach game with a small ball (Bačvice beach). In summer every year there is a world championship in picigin.

candidates.name: Grgur Ninski
candidates.content: It is said that if you touch the big toe of the statue and make a wish your wish will come true.

candidates.name: Gaga Bar
candidates.content: Cosy atmosphere, long list of cocktails, Latin music. Ask for a bill, because one round is €14, and then second one (the same one) may be €20. Atmosphere is nice, but the waiters are not. More tourists than locals.

candidates.name: Sanctuary Bar
candidates.content: The beachhead of craft cocktails in Split, with a selection of craft beers as well. Run by US expat, Tristan.

candidates.name: Vanilla Club
candidates.content: Fancy place by the swimming pool with popular domestic and foreign music.

candidates.name: St Riva
candidates.content: Has an upper story that overlooks the promenade.

candidates.name: Zlatna ribica
candidates.content: Great local spot for delicious seafood. Friendly staff. Not many tables so you may have to wait for an available table.

candidates.name: Theatrum Bar & Food
candidates.content: Reservation can be made via email, phone or social media. Dine in, curbside-pickup, delivery, seating, Wi-Fi, fresh ingredients, breakfast, dinner, lunch.

candidates.name: Fino i Friško 2 - Biškić
candidates.content: Because of its proximity to school, this bakery always has fresh and tasty food.

candidates.name: Kod Joze
candidates.content: The traditional family-run konoba serves tasty dishes in style. Prices very reasonable considering the quality and atmosphere.

candidates.name: Biser Orijenta
candidates.content: Good "European Chinese" cuisine. Not too popular among the locals, but the prices are fair and the service is friendly.

candidates.name: Kod Sfinge Vanevropske Zviri
candidates.content: A Konoba/Trattoria. Good Dalmatian specialties: Pašticada, Paški sir, etc. Also proposes good seafood catch of the day, but sometimes unavailable. Seems to be operated by a single family: The waiters knows very well the menu!

candidates.name: Fife
candidates.content: Lively and busy restaurant with lots of seating and deliciously large Croatian dishes.

candidates.name: Pizza Cut Planet 1
candidates.content: A good offer for those who want to try several types of pizzas without buying them completely. Great pizza idea. Several flavours to choose from.

candidates.name: Vege
candidates.content: Delicious and fresh vegan food. The best veggies in Split. Good atmosphere and homemade food made live.

candidates.name: Sandwich Bar Rizzo
candidates.content: The best sandwiches in Split. Always fresh food and very helpful staff.

candidates.name: Ba!Će
candidates.content: Balkan atmosphere. Ba!Cevapi is their flagship dish, which consists of minced meat, well spiced and grilled, served with typical bread and sauces

candidates.name: Pizzeria Kaleta
candidates.content: Freshly baked dough, crispy just as it should be, chicken and hearty side dishes. Great pizza

candidates.name: Pazar
candidates.content: Farmers market with perfect fruit, vegetables and more. The best time to visit the market is Saturday or Sunday morning.

candidates.name: Ribarnica
candidates.content: Fresh fish market.

december.text: Marjan - a hill situated on the west of Split. Marjan is an oasis for many people who look for a natural stress relief, a great place for long walks, jogging, and bike rides. Marjan's peak, Telegrin is 178 m high and gives a wonderful panoramic view of Split. South cliffs are popular within alpine climbers. St. Nichola
